← type me it

models

48 trials · updated 22 october 2026

every model we've tried against the one type me it runs, tested on our own dictations and meetings. accuracy comes first, then speed, then memory and cpu, then download size - a new model has to match on accuracy before the rest count.

these notes are written by ai from evals we run ad hoc on a MacBook Pro (Apple M4, 10-core CPU, 24 GB, macOS 26). we would love it if you have any models you suggest we test (hello@typeme.it) - the point of type me it is to make onboarding as minimal as possible, so we want to use the best local model for each category instead of giving you even more decision fatigue.

  • speech recognitionParakeet Ultra4.09% dictation · 12.55% meetings
  • clean-upApple on-device model326 of 335 eval cases
  • speakersNemotron 3 Diarization4.8% of words on the wrong speaker

speech recognition

22 october 2026

Underdog Bark 3.0 Pro

rejected

dictation tied at 4.22%; meetings 13.12% vs Ultra's 12.65%, with 508 deleted words to Ultra's 230

notes

Underdog Bark 3.0 Pro (Conway Research, published 2026-10-15: English fine-tune of Parakeet TDT v3 at full precision; FP16 Core ML, 1.23 GB, one encoder package with short8 and full15 functions; CC-BY-4.0), through fluidasr bark-pro (FluidAudio 0.17.5, .ultra, the maker's runner settings)

against
FluidAudio Parakeet Ultra (fluid-ultra, same 62 clips)
expected
Meetings 0.3–1.0 points better than Ultra (claimed AMI-Cleaned 7.16 against v3's 9.42; same architecture, English fine-tune at full precision), dictation a tie. Predicted p95 150–200 ms, 1.3–1.6 GB resident (risk to the 1.5 GB dictation budget), Neural Engine, 1.23 GB file (2× Ultra). Wrong if meetings are not more than 0.2 points better, or dictation is more than 0.2 points worse
measured
WER vs AssemblyAI Universal-3.5 Pro, unprompted (ASSEMBLYAI_PROMPT=''; the verbatim-prompted references are not built), 50 dictations and 12 meeting tracks, 24 spans hand-checked, with and without fillers; S/D/I per track; p50/p95; peak memory; CPU and GPU %
result
Dictation 4.17% vs 4.32% (29 vs 30 errors); fillers dropped 4.22% vs 4.22%. Meetings 14.11% vs 13.20%; fillers dropped 13.12% vs 12.65% (+0.47). 508 deletions vs 230, worse on 8 of 12 tracks; on one 24 s room clip it writes 27 of about 70 words, leaving out quieter background speech, and the first 14 s alone lose the same words, so it is the model, not chunking. Fewer insertions (717 vs 980), which the listen review found are mostly real speech for Ultra. Dictation p50/p95 59/125 ms vs 57/131 ms, same session. Peak resident 1,094 MiB on the first run, while the Neural Engine compiled the encoder, vs 643 MiB for Ultra's; 146 vs 120 MiB once compiled. The first compile took 99 min; later loads 0.3 s. Meetings 142× vs 240× realtime. CPU 104% vs 123% mean, GPU 22% vs 7% mean (Neural Engine for both). Not a quiet Mac: Spotlight indexing at ~340% CPU, another session's script at 100%, GPU baseline 25–67%
held
no: meetings 0.47 points worse
verdict
rejected

18 october 2026

Parakeet vs Ultra on meaning

open

on meaning, Parakeet's meeting WER is 8.04% against Ultra's 9.45%

notes

Parakeet (transcribe.cpp Q8_0, shipped before Ultra) against FluidAudio Parakeet Ultra (shipped), on meaning

expected
Parakeet's 1.5-point lead over Ultra against the Universal-3.5 Pro reference is the reference's tidying, not meaning
measured
Meaning WER (Opus 5.5 labelled all 1,814 disputed spans; errors counted only where the meaning changes), then 39 blind picks of which reading was said, 13 from each group: reference agrees with Parakeet, with Ultra, or with neither
result
Meaning WER: Parakeet 8.04%, Ultra 9.45% (meetings); 0.86% vs 1.58% (dictation). Picks: where the reference agreed with Parakeet it was right 8 of 13 (Ultra 2, none 3); with Ultra, 7 of 13 (Parakeet 4); all differ: reference 5, Parakeet 4, Ultra 2, none 2. Extrapolated, Ultra makes 256 more meaning errors than Parakeet (+1.49 points) against 240 (+1.40) by the reference alone
held
no: the lead is real
verdict
open: Parakeet is more accurate on meaning; switching back trades Ultra's speed (2.9× faster dictation p95), idle GPU and 310 MB for it. Answers kept as truths and in Scripts/asr-eval/vault/truths.tmv

Fluid Speech Mini

open

dictation tied with Ultra at 4.09%; room tracks 10.42% vs 9.12% with fillers dropped

notes

Fluid Speech Mini (FluidVoice, published 2026-10-13: Parakeet TDT v3 encoder fine-tuned for dictation and to ignore a second voice, Parakeet Ultra's decoder and joint, ~3-bit Core ML weights; CC-BY-4.0). Core ML package through fluidasr local (FluidAudio 0.17.5 loadLocal, .v3)

against
FluidAudio Parakeet Ultra (shipped), re-timed in the same session
expected
Dictation ties Ultra within 0.2 points (same architecture, dictation fine-tune); meetings tie on mic tracks, with a risk that training it to follow one speaker drops the other people on room and others tracks. Predicted p95 ~100 ms, ~280 MB, 2.4× smaller download; if accuracy ties, download size is the axis it wins
measured
WER vs AssemblyAI Universal-2 reference, 50 dictations and 12 meeting tracks, 0 spans hand-checked, with and without fillers; S/D/I per track type; p50/p95; peak memory; CPU and GPU %
result
Dictation 4.09% vs 4.09% (28 errors each); fillers dropped 2.92% vs 3.07%. Meetings 15.52% vs 14.58%; fillers dropped 13.66% vs 13.46% (+0.20, the edge of the tie). By track, fillers dropped: mic 15.34% vs 15.40%, others 11.76% vs 11.76%, room 10.42% vs 9.12% (58 deletions vs 33). Fewer insertions overall (942 vs 1,225), which the listen review showed are mostly real speech for Ultra. Dictation p50/p95 43/91 ms vs 51/105 ms; meetings 183× vs 240× realtime; peak 288 vs 301 MiB on meetings; CPU 166% vs 178% mean, GPU 29% vs 32% mean (Neural Engine for both; another session's dev app held the GPU at 33–55% throughout); 253 vs 613 MB download
held
partly: dictation and mic tie, room tracks lose words as feared
verdict
open: listen-review the room-track and mic-insertion spans where it and Ultra differ, and rescore against Universal-3.5 Pro once those references are built

CTC vocabulary boosting on Ultra

rejected

synthetic term hits up to 99% from 78%, dictation WER up to 8.18% from 4.67%, p95 3.1× slower

notes

FluidAudio CTC vocabulary boosting (parakeet-ctc-110m, VocabularyBoostingSession.rescore) on Parakeet Ultra, with and without CustomWordMatcher

against
Ultra + CustomWordMatcher (the app; meetings apply no custom words)
expected
Boosting raises custom-word accuracy without other-word WER rising over 0.2 points; risk is speed (~3.4× slower earlier, which would put Ultra's 97 ms p95 over 300 ms)
measured
15 custom words (10 with aliases); 50 real dictations (2 carry a custom word), 12 meeting tracks (2 carry one), 90 synthesised say term sentences; hit rate, WER, false insertions, p50/p95, N× realtime
result
Synth hits 53% plain, 78% A, 99% boosted, 100% boosted + matcher. Dictation WER 4.67% A vs 8.18% boosted, p50/p95 51/117 ms A vs 169/359 ms boosted (3.3×/3.1× slower), 26 false insertions vs 5. Meetings WER 15.22% A vs 18.57% boosted, 227× vs 58× realtime. Needs a second model, 101 MB
held
speed yes (3.1× slower, over the 300 ms p95); custom-word gain yes on synthetic speech; other-word WER no
verdict
rejected
12 october 2026

Custom-word matcher retuned for Ultra

shipped

0 false insertions and dictation WER 4.09%, same as plain Ultra; 71% of synthetic term hits

notes

CustomWordMatcher retuned for Parakeet Ultra: dictionary words are not replaced on sound alone, a confident word does not join an unsure one in a run, +0.05 sound bar per extra word

against
CustomWordMatcher as tuned on transcribe.cpp confidences
expected
Retuned thresholds bring false insertions to about 0 and real-dictation WER to within 0.2 points of plain Ultra (4.29% or less) while keeping 70% or more of synthetic term hits
measured
15 custom words (10 with aliases); 50 real dictations (2 carry one), 12 meeting tracks, 90 synthesised say term sentences; clips split by hash parity into tune and held-out halves, sweep on tune, report on held-out; WER, hits, false insertions
result
Thresholds alone could not do it: the 5 real and 1 synthetic false insertions were all unsure words (confidence 0.5 to 0.68) with sound keys equal or one edit away, and the correct words Ultra scores that low (5% under 0.75, 34 of 669) look the same, so no confidence or similarity setting separated them. Three structural rules did: 2 of the 5 were dictionary words, 3 were a confident word carried into a term by an unsure neighbour (2 words each), and the run penalty cut multi-word meeting false matches 31 to 14. After: dictation WER 4.09% (plain Ultra 4.09%, was 4.67%), 0 false insertions real and synthetic, synthetic hits 64/90 (71%, was 70/90), real hits 0/2 (unchanged). Held-out: WER 3.57% both, 0 false, synthetic 35/49 (71%). Meetings: 14 false matches over 16,674 words against 2 for plain Ultra (99 before); 10 of the 14 come from stored aliases, and with aliases off it is 6. Matcher with dictionary check p95 1.2 ms
held
yes: false insertions 0, WER 4.09% (within 0.2), synthetic hits 71%; meetings not safe while aliases apply
verdict
shipped (branch matcher-ultra-thresholds)
